newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary repo cut no surprise, more seen - traders.
newsitem.headline: Hungary repo cut no surprise, more seen - traders.

text.p: Monday's repo rate cuts by Hungary's central bank did not surprise the market which expects one more 0.25 percentage points cut until the end of 1996, traders said.
"It was about time for this cut to happen," Sandor Tolonics of Budapest Bank told Reuters.
The National Bank of Hungary (NBH) cut four of its five repo rates by 0.25 percentage points each on Monday, confirming market expectations and leaving only the overnight reverse repo unchanged. @

Last Friday overnight rates surged to 28.50 percent from the usual 22 to 23 percent range in tight liquidity, as market players, expecting an imminent rate cut, tied up all available amounts in the NBH's one-week reverse repo facility.
Traders said another repo rate cut was likely before the end of the year.
"Today's cut was expected somewhat earlier and I see another 0.25 percent point cut until the end of the year," said Balazs Varga of Inter-Europa Bank. @

However, Zsolt Kovari of ING Bank said he expected today's cut somewhat later. He also sees the most popular one-week reverse repo rate, currently standing at 22.75 percent, to bottom out at around 22 percent.
Traders agreed that the repo rates are approaching a limit where forint savings might become less attractive, leaving the central bank little room to manouevre.
Hungary's forint has a crawling peg devaluation rate of 1.2 percentage points per month and according to recent Finance Ministry statements changes are unlikely in the short term. @
The NBH last cut the same rates by 0.25 percentage points on August 5, which only came as a surprise because of its timing, rather than its size.

The NBH's overnight and one-week repo rates were today set at 28.75 percent, the one-week reverse repo at 22.75 percent and the one-month reverse repo at 23.25 percent. The overnight reverse repo rate remained unchanged at 17.50 percent.
